newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks capture light gains by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks capture light gains by close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2508 +19 US 30yr cl 6.92 -0.04
10yrbond futs 92.115 +0.070 Gold NY 340.40 Lon fix 339.25
*Stocks lock in single figure gains by the close, traders trim gains ahead of U.S. jobs data. Vol 273.58 million, A$712.51 million value, 1,056 stocks traded, 337 steady, 384 up, 335 down.
A resilient Australian share market locked in light single figure gains by the close on Friday as traders battened down for U.S. payroll data due later today.
The All Ordinaries index added 6.20 points to 2,491.6.
June share price index futures were up 19 points at 2,508, a 16.4 point premium to the underlying index.

While some early strength surprised, taking the market as much as 12 points higher at one stage, the pre-weekend profit-taking that sapped gains in the afternoon did not, with traders preferring to go into the weekend uncommitted.

"The rise early on was the surprise rather than the afternoon profit-taking, but that is usually the case on Friday afternoon - people want to clean up the books," said head of equities at Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely.
Sekely remained confident, though, about the market's level of support, with few problems on the horizon at this stage.
"The market has done a very good job indeed. I can't see too much out there to worry about."
Local retail trade figures for March failed to impact, with traders saying they had alreaduy been factored into the market.

Among the large capitalisation stocks, Westpac Banking Corporation was the performer, its shares ending over two percent higher at A$7.05 after it announced a plan to buyback 50 million shares or about 2.8 percent of its issued capital.
Bank sector leader National Australia Bank was also popular early, briefly touching a record high A$17.81 before profit takers pushed it back to A$17.70 by the close, still up 13.7 cents.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to seven, while about 36 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures saw reasonable activity with the widening premium generating some interest and driving the underlying market higher mid-morning. Options trade was slow.
Total options traded 26,581 (31,294)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 7,024 (6,248)
In other local markets, Australian bond yields ended lower as the market squared up ahead of the key U.S. non-farm payrolls report and after a volatile trading week which saw easing hopes evaporate.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.86 percent, down Thursday's 7.94 percent.
The Australian dollar spent the day ensconced in a comfortable range as the market took stock after amassing a cent of gains this week.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the currency had settled at US$0.7838/43 after see-sawing in a US$0.7825/7853 range through the day, having finished Thursday at US$0.7747/52.
